title: Home Values and Firm Behavior
summary_en: How big is the link between the housing market and small-firm investment? Bahaj, Foulis and Pintér use UK micro-data to show that a £1 rise in the home value of a firm's directors lifts the firm's wage bill by about 3p, with similar effects on investment and employment, and the mechanism is collateral: directors borrow against their homes to fund their businesses. Aggregate house-price swings therefore feed directly into corporate behaviour through entrepreneurs' personal balance sheets.
data_used: UK firm–director linked microdata combining Companies House director records, individual property holdings via the Land Registry, and firm financials. Identification exploits within-director and within-region variation in residential house prices.
policy_relevance: Speaks directly to Hungarian SME credit and housing-market policy. Many Hungarian small-business owners pledge homes as collateral; macroprudential changes from the MNB (LTV / DSTI tightening) and Garantiqa-style state guarantees therefore have a second-order effect on the corporate sector that is rarely modelled. Suggests Hungarian SME-finance interventions (széchenyi-kártya, MFB programmes) should be evaluated against the home-collateral channel, not just bank-credit metrics.
